metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to code changes submitted as contributions; AI tool must be disclosed and human must fully understand the code.
domains.accountability_holder: The contributing individual (the human-in-the-loop who must understand and can explain the code)

evidence.quote: All AI usage in any form must be disclosed. You must state the tool you used
The human-in-the-loop must fully understand all code. If you can't explain what your changes do

domains.reasoning: The policy names code contributions directly, requires disclosure of the AI tool used, and mandates a human-in-the-loop who must fully understand and be able to explain the code, placing accountability on the contributor who submits it.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of meeting/notetaker bot use or supervision
domains.reasoning: The policy contains no reference to recorded meetings, notetaker bots, or AI transcription/summarization of discussions.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: AI-generated media only (art, images, videos, audio, etc.); text is allowed subject to other rules in the policy

evidence.quote: No AI-generated media is allowed (art, images, videos, audio, etc.). Text and code are the only acceptable AI-generated content, per the other rules in this policy.

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder named for content/media rule; documentation and blogs not named
domains.reasoning: The policy explicitly bans AI-generated media (art, images, video, audio) but does not name documentation or blogs specifically, and does not state who is accountable for a violation of the media ban beyond the general enforcement mechanism (denouncement list), which is enforcement, not authorship accountability.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI use in moderation actions
domains.reasoning: The denouncement-list clause addresses consequences for bad AI-assisted contributions but says nothing about AI being used to perform moderation actions (e.g., auto-flagging, auto-banning); that is an enforcement mechanism against contributors, not a statement about AI-driven moderation.

evidence.quote: Every discussion, issue, and pull request is read and reviewed by humans (and sometimes machines, too).

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level or accountability holder for AI-assisted review
domains.reasoning: The policy names review activity and acknowledges machines sometimes participate in reviewing discussions/PRs, but sets no supervision level, scope limit, or accountability holder for that machine review.

evidence.quote: The human-in-the-loop must fully understand all code.
any content generated with AI must have been reviewed _and edited_ by a human before submission

domains.suggested_improvement: no explicit rule naming autonomous/agentic AI use; no accountability holder
domains.reasoning: The policy never names 'autonomous' or 'agentic' AI use directly. It is only reached indirectly through the general human-in-the-loop requirements applied to code and to issues/discussions, which implicitly disallow unsupervised agentic submissions, but no accountability holder or scope is stated for autonomous use specifically.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of environmental impact anywhere in policy
domains.reasoning: The document never raises energy, water, hardware, or carbon-footprint concerns as rationale or rule.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of infrastructure or server-load impact
domains.reasoning: There is no discussion of infrastructure strain, server load, or hardware cost anywhere in the policy.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of training-data provenance or usage
domains.reasoning: The policy does not discuss the data used to train the AI tools contributors employ, nor any concerns about copyright or provenance of training data.

unscoped_statements.quote: All AI usage in any form must be disclosed.
Maintainers are exempt from these rules and may use AI tools at their discretion; they've proven themselves trustworthy to apply good judgment.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: Ghostty's AI policy is fairly specific about code contributions and text-based issues/discussions (requiring disclosure and a human-in-the-loop who fully understands the work) and explicitly bans AI-generated media, but it never names notetaker bots, moderation, environmental impact, infrastructure strain, or training data, and only glancingly touches review and autonomous/agentic use through general human-in-the-loop language without stating accountability holders for those areas.

validation_problems: code_contributions: quote not found in AI_POLICY.md
code_contributions: quote not found in AI_POLICY.md
content: quote not found in AI_POLICY.md

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
